      <title>UK sanctions Sudanese military leaders implicated in El Fasher ‘campaign of rape’</title>

      <description><p>Commanders suspected of sexual violence during the largest and fastest slaughter of civilians in more than 30 years have been subjected to travel ban and asset freeze</p><p>Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/mar/25/heroism-horror-and-the-pits-of-hell-inside-the-last-days-of-el-fasher">mass atrocity</a> that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days.</p><p>A year after the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2025/nov/02/he-told-the-world-what-was-happening-in-el-fasher-then-they-sought-him-out-how-sudan-lost-a-true-hero-of-the-war">fall of El Fasher</a>, the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/26/uk-sanctions-sudanese-military-leaders-implicated-in-el-fasher-campaign-of">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 15:58:51 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Jordan arrests three following deadly terror attack on church</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261026-jordan-arrests-three-following-deadly-terror-attack-on-church</link><description>
Jordanian authorities on Monday arrested three terrorists following a deadly attack on a church during a funeral procession that killed nine people in the western village of Hammoud. The three assailants – who are Islamic extremists, according the Jordanian director of public security – were injured in a dawn shootout with authorities and are due to be brought before the courts in the nation that supports capital punishment.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/94116308-d06c-11f1-88fd-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/b65b319e54017e17feaa4f11998604f254a999a2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/94116308-d06c-11f1-88fd-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/b65b319e54017e17feaa4f11998604f254a999a2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2ded65f4-d14d-11f1-acd0-7d88c33f0f1f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 15:12:52 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/94116308-d06c-11f1-88fd-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/b65b319e54017e17feaa4f11998604f254a999a2.jpg">© Ahmad Shoura, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Brazil's Lula reelected president in runoff vote: A look back at his career</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/brazil-s-lula-reelected-president-in-runoff-vote-a-look-back-at-his-career</link><description>
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won an unprecedented fourth term on Sunday (October 25), the country's electoral court said, in a shock result that defied polls.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fd221fee-d13a-11f1-84ec-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4EJ8VV.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fd221fee-d13a-11f1-84ec-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4EJ8VV.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">01bf2c78-d14e-11f1-b175-4ba06036b7bc</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 15:11:20 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>US Midterms 2026: A history of gerrymandering</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/us-midterms-2026-a-history-of-gerrymandering</link><description>
What does a salamander have to do with US elections? Dating back centuries, gerrymandering continues to play a role in American elections today. Used more often by Republicans in the modern era of voting, Democrats have also resorted to the tactic in the past decade. But what is gerrymandering, and why is it called that? FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha explains.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a8ee3dee-d14a-11f1-9245-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/Thumbnail-01-Gerrymandering.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a8ee3dee-d14a-11f1-9245-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/Thumbnail-01-Gerrymandering.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dcbf3ec0-d14a-11f1-9017-e7dfd85b688e</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 14:48:54 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Macron promises 'concrete measures' in response to French students' demands</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261026-french-president-promises-concrete-measures-in-response-to-french-students-demands</link><description>

SpaceX is shooting for new heights with its upcoming Starship test flight, and the booster tapped for the mission is in its final stretch of preparations before the mission.

The Super Heavy booster for Flight Test 15, Booster 22, underwent a static test fire on Sunday (Oct. 25), igniting all of its Raptor 3 engines for about 15 seconds. "Full duration 33-engine static fire for the Super Heavy booster preparing for Flight 15," SpaceX said in a post on X.

The test is a beginning of final checks on the first-stage vehicle, which will be mated with the Flight 15 upper stage, Ship 42, ahead of launch, but not before the spacecraft completes some tests of its own.

Ship 42 will also complete a series of tests as the next Starship launch approaches, including a static engine fire and final systems checks. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has stated that SpaceX will attempt the first launch tower catch of a ship upper stage on Flight 15, which, if successful, would be a significant step forward for the company's goal to mature Starship to full reusability.

SpaceX's confidence in its ability to catch both the Super Heavy and Ship stages has been building this year, following three launches so far in 2026. Its most recent (Sept. 28) mission, Flight 14, reached orbit for the first time and performed the successful deployment of 26 next-generation Starlink V3 satellites, marking the first operational payloads delivered to orbit by the spacecraft. Starlink V3 satellites are too big to fit aboard the company's workhorse Falcon 9 rocket.

Flight 14 wasn't without setbacks, however. An upper-stage Raptor engine shut down prematurely during ascent, prompting SpaceX to cut the planned 10-hour mission short. Ship, nevertheless, completed a controlled reentry and splashed down in the Pacific Ocean about three hours after liftoff.

Flight 15 could carry another batch of V3 Starlinks, though SpaceX has not officially confirmed a payload. Beginning to upgrade its global network with the fast V3 satellites, however, is a major reason SpaceX is pushing to bring Starship into regular service.

Starship's development also has implications for NASA's Artemis program, which has contracted SpaceX to develop a modified Ship upper stage capable of landing astronauts on the surface of the moon.

NASA recently updated the timeline of milestones SpaceX needs to accomplish with Starship before a lunar lander version will qualify to carry crews, with a significant demonstration mission coming up next summer on Artemis III.

The next Artemis mission will launch astronauts to Earth orbit aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft, which will dock with both lunar lander vehicles over the course of about two weeks (in addition to Starship, NASA contracted Blue Origin's Blue Moon spacecraft as a another lunar lander for the program).

SpaceX is also working toward an uncrewed lunar landing demonstration ahead of NASA's planned return of astronauts to the moon on Artemis IV, targeted for 2028. Which lander will be chosen for that mission is still undetermined, and SpaceX and Blue Origin are both still vying for the first crewed Artemis landing.

Beyond Flight 15, SpaceX hopes to demonstrate additional milestones before the end of 2026, including Starship's first launch from Florida and potentially the first re-flight of an upgraded V3 Super Heavy booster.

Booster 22's engine test marks the beginning in a series of tests leading up Flight 15, which, if recent Starship campaigns are any example, could lift off sometime in mid-to-late November.

]]> <![CDATA[ Glowing 'cauldron' of new stars | Space photo of the day for Oct. 26, 2026 ]]>

The NASA/ESA James Webb Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of a majestic star-forming region shining 161,000 light-years from Earth in a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way known as the Large Magellanic Cloud.

What is it?

The deep-space image reveals a 230-light-year-wide swathe of the glowing emission nebula N159, threaded with denser filaments of reddish molecular hydrogen that hide countless energetic young stars.

Ghostly blue clouds of ionized hydrogen gas (H II) glow in the center of the image, having been energized by the ultraviolet radiation pouring out from nearby stars, whose winds helped create the chaotic structure of the vast stellar nursery.

The ethereal pockets are surrounded by roiling orange clouds of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons — a type of organic molecule that may account for 30% of all carbon in the universe, according to the U.S. Department of Energy.

Why is it incredible?

N159 is estimated to be less than 3 million years old, making it one of the youngest star-forming regions in the Large Magellanic Cloud. It also has a markedly different composition than the stellar nurseries that spawn stars in our Milky Way, boasting a lower metal content that could mirror environments that existed in the early universe.

By pointing JWST at N159, astronomers open a window to the distant past. They can compare the characteristics of stars at varying stages of evolution, including pre-main-sequence stars that are still in the process of forming, or accreting from the vast interstellar cloud.

Want to know more?

]]> <![CDATA[ Rubin telescope should find more of Earth's mysterious 'mini-moons' — including some we can study up close ]]> Earth almost always has more than one moon. The others are just very small, and they never stay long — but they could provide accessible and unique insights into the solar system.

Temporary satellites, or mini-moons, are small asteroids that wander into Earth’s neighborhood and get captured briefly by our planet’s gravity. A typical one stays about nine months and circles Earth roughly three times before escaping back into orbit around the sun, Grigori Fedorets of Finland's University of Helsinki said in a presentation at the Europlanet Science Congress (EPSC) 2026 in The Hague in September.

Fedorets' modeling suggests that the largest mini-moon around Earth at any given moment is typically only about 75 centimeters (30 inches) across. An asteroid about 3 meters (10 feet) wide should be captured every 10 to 20 years.

"This is not just a theoretical construct. There is observational evidence," Fedorets said. Only two mini-moons have been confirmed to date, however — 2006 RH120 and 2020 CD3, both discovered by the Catalina Sky Survey in Arizona. Two fireballs, seen over the Czech Republic in 2013 and Australia in 2016, were traced back to objects that had been in geocentric orbits. Two more asteroids, 2022 NX1 and 2024 PT5, were captured only briefly, without completing a full orbit.

Fedorets noted a potential third mini-moon — the recently detected Sar2901, which could also be an artificial object. Sar2901 has since faded from view but should be observable again around mid-to-late November, according to the Minor Planet Center.

Small rocks, big questions

Mini-moons are so small that scientists know little about them. For objects between 1 and 10 meters (3.3 to 33 feet) across, models of the near-Earth asteroid population disagree with the numbers suggested by records of fireballs in Earth's atmosphere. Mini-moons sit right in that gap, so finding more of them should show which picture is right.

They may also reveal how much of the material in Earth’s neighborhood traces its origin back to our moon, as some small asteroids may be chunks of the lunar surface blasted into space by impacts. During the temporary flyby of asteroid 2024 PT5, for example, scientists found its spectrum to be closer to lunar rock than to typical asteroids, according to a 2025 study led by Theodore Kareta, which Fedorets described as the strongest evidence yet for lunar ejecta among Earth's small neighbors.

Kamo’oalewa, a much larger asteroid and quasi-moon of Earth, at which China’s Tianwen-2 mission arrived in July, has been the subject of debate over possible lunar or asteroidal origins.

Rubin game-changer and budget sample returns

The transformative Vera C. Rubin Observatory's 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) should find many more mini-moons, though further work will be needed. On its own, Fedorets estimates, the survey should catch a mini-moon about once every two years.

Fedorets and colleagues are setting up a dedicated system running on a virtual server at Finland's Center for Scientific Computing, to sift Rubin's alerts through the ANTARES real-time astronomical data broker to flag potential mini-moons for follow-up observations, which could raise detections to two or three per year.

Making regular discoveries could open doors for future missions, providing targets for relatively easy, low-cost asteroid sample-return missions. Mini-moons’ proximity to Earth, and their low relative speeds, means less rocket propellant is needed to get out to these diminutive targets and back to Earth.

Initially, Fedorets envisions cubesat tech demo missions, which would pave the way for mid-sized missions that could collect samples. He sees the Tianwen-2 low-energy sample mission as a potential stepping stone to resource utilization, while also noting that, at the higher end of the scale, there have been programs such as NASA’s cancelled Asteroid Redirect Mission (ARM) and plans by, for example, TransAstra to put a 100-ton asteroid into a stable orbit around Earth.

"This is not sci-fi," Fedorets said. "These people are actually thinking about this kind of stuff."

The short warning times and instability of the orbits of mini-moons dictates potential mission profiles. A spacecraft could wait in Earth-moon space, ready to head for a newly found mini-moon, similar to how ESA's Comet Interceptor will launch and then wait for a suitable comet to study. Asteroids could also be nudged into more stable orbits, allowing more extensive future missions.

"LSST is now online, and over the next 10 years, we are expected to find many more of these temporary moons," Fedorets said. Regular discoveries could pave the way for exploration in the early 2030s and sampling missions later in the decade.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'More missions, more often': NASA is overhauling how it selects science missions ]]> NASA is overhauling how it selects and develops science missions, with changes intended to reduce costs, streamline competition and get missions into space faster.

The changes, directed by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, could significantly reshape how scientists, universities, NASA centers and commercial companies vie for future missions.

"We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long," Fox stated in the letter.

The new process aims to prioritize scientific merit over unduly complicated engineering and financial planning during initial evaluations, and reduce selection timelines to encourage innovation.

Fox and other top NASA science officials will provide an overview of the reforms during a virtual town hall today (Oct. 26) at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT). A livestream of the event will be available here, with an opportunity for the public to submit questions here.

NASA currently selects many of its science missions through competitive Announcements of Opportunity (AOs), inviting scientists and research institutions to submit proposals. Under the existing two-step process, competing teams must include thorough engineering and financial details as part of their proposals before NASA selects finalists for further study. The process can take almost three years, requiring significant investments of time and resources from teams that may ultimately never get selected.

CM 2.0 aims to reduce that burden by emphasizing scientific distinction during initial evaluations, allowing teams to defer much of the engineering and financial planning until later. Instead, initial proposals will focus on the scientific objectives of a mission and a preliminary plan for how to accomplish them.

NASA organizes its science missions into different classes based on their size, cost and objectives, with selection procedures varying between them. These range from smaller Explorer missions to large, expensive flagships like the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

Under CM 2.0, programs including smaller Discovery planetary missions, larger New Frontiers spacecraft and Astro-Probes, a program that focuses on mid-sized astronomy missions, will retain a streamlined version of the existing two-step process, but with nearly half of the material required for initial proposals. "This means that the original 35-months timeline will be reduced to about 19.5 months, all while having a stronger, more mature mission at the time of selection," Fox wrote.

Flagship missions, meanwhile, will continue following their current procedures, which were recently revised based on lessons learned from a study of best practices examining the development of JWST.

Medium-class Explorer (MIDEX) and Earth Explorer missions will open to a wider range of applicants, including universities and commercial organizations, and will have similar changes implemented for their two-step selection process. NASA plans to evaluate prospective mission developers based on their track records with projects of similar size, cost and complexity, and offer principal investigator-led teams the opportunity to request support from NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center or Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) during the first stage of selection.

Smaller, lower-cost science programs will see a more substantial selection process shakeup. "Our smallest missions will be riding the momentum of a maturing commercial space economy and will move even faster," Fox wrote.

Under CM 2.0, these programs will move to a single-stage selection process, eliminating the need for a second round of competing proposals entirely.

These include the Small Explorer (SMEX) and Earth Venture missions, which conduct astronomy and heliophysics research, and targeted studies of Earth and its climate. Missions of Opportunity, which allow researchers to piggyback scientific investigations onto other missions, as well as hosted payloads and rideshares, will fall under the same one-step umbrella, which is expected to drop final selection timelines from approximately 32 months to just 19.

"Breaches of control thresholds will carry real consequences," Fox wrote, adding that such consequences could include mission cancellations in the face of unmet expectations.

The longer-term outcome of the new approach, the agency hopes, will reduce the financial and technical burden on competing research teams and ultimately get missions from idea to orbit with efficiency and speed.

"This is a moment of real opportunity," Fox wrote. "We have an administrator who is empowering us to move faster and a commercial market that is ready to help. On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Iapetus was the second moon anyone had ever found orbiting Saturn, and it was the first of four moons Cassini would discover at the ringed planet.

The Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens had discovered Titan, the largest of Saturn's moons, about six years earlier. After Cassini found Iapetus, he also found the moons Rhea, Tethys and Dione.

When Cassini first saw Iapetus, the moon looked like a tiny speck on the west side of Saturn. He calculated its orbit and thought he would be able to see it again on the east side of Saturn 39 days later, but it was nowhere to be seen. When it reappeared on the west side again, Cassini realized that Iapetus must be darker on one side than the other, which made it harder to see when the dark side was facing Earth.

More than 300 years later, NASA sent a spacecraft named Cassini to Saturn, and that Cassini took some pretty awesome photos of Iapetus. Realizing Iapetus kind of resembled a yin-yang, it has since been nicknamed the "yin-yang moon."

How it mattered

The discovery of Iapetus, with its yin-yang bright and dark hemispheres, has added to our understanding of how moons form.

"Using the computer simulations, the researchers concluded ... the inner moons of Saturn and its gorgeous rings are all relatively young. The more distant moons Titan and Iapetus would not have been formed at the same time."

"Our best guess is that Saturn had a similar collection of moons before, but their orbits were disturbed by a special kind of orbital resonance involving Saturn's motion around the sun. Eventually, the orbits of neighboring moons crossed, and these objects collided. From this rubble, the present set of moons and rings formed."

The October full moon rises tonight! Here's everything you need to know about the "Hunter's Moon," including where to see it, how it got its name and other tricks of the light and mind that could conspire to create a truly spectacular lunar light show.

October's moon reaches 100% illumination at 12:12 a.m. EDT (0412 GMT) on Oct. 26, as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. The shadowy terminator that separates the day and night side of the moon is conspicuously absent around this time, as are the shadows that throw craters into spectacular relief during the waxing and waning lunar phases.

Instead, it's a perfect time to explore the dark lunar "seas" that cover the moon's surface where lava flooded impact basins billions of years ago, before hardening to create enormous basaltic plains. Streaks of reflective material can also be spotted streaking away from bright young craters, where material from the lunar subsurface was excavated and cast across the moon's surface during brutal asteroid impacts.

Where and when to see the October full moon.

Stargazers in the U.S. will get their first view of the full moon as it climbs into the eastern sky at sunset on Oct. 25. Be sure to check out Time and Date's moonrise tracker to discover the exact timings for your location.

The moon often appears particularly large while close to the horizon, thanks to a phenomenon called the "Moon Effect," wherein our brains trick us into thinking that the lunar disk is larger while in close visual proximity to the ground than it is when overhead.

The moon can also take on a spectacular yellow-orange color in the hour after moonrise, as blue wavelengths of its reflected light — the shortest in the visible spectrum — are scattered during its oblique passage through Earth's atmosphere.

Why is the October full moon called the "Hunter's Moon"?

October's full moon is commonly known as the Hunter's Moon in the Northern Hemisphere because it rises soon after farmers have cleared away the summer's harvest, leaving the fields bare for hunters to catch their prey and prepare it as food for the winter, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac.

It's also called the "Migrating Moon" by the North American Cree people, in reference to the birds that travel to warmer climates around the time of its rising. The Ojibwe and the Haida know it asthe "Freezing Moon," to reflect the drop in temperature that occurs in autumn.

On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space.

While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before.

The ability to photograph Earth from space drove both an expanded interest to continue pushing into space and led to unexpected societal changes with regards to how humanity considered its home planet.

For military and intelligence agencies, the potential now existed for reconnaissance at a far larger scale than what was possible with high-altitude aircraft. That capability expanded to agriculture and meteorological purposes, eventually making Earth observation one of the most common reasons satellites and space stations are deployed into orbit today.

Earth photography from space also gave birth to the environmental movement, as people began to see the planet differently. The fragility of this orb became more apparent, as now Earth appeared a "blue marble" set against an endless black void.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks ]]> It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of "Star Trek" before it. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say.

That should trouble any Trekkie. "Star Trek" — a show built on progressive ideals, thoughtful characters, and boundary-breaking television — was completely and totally afraid to say anything at all.

Mash it up, Scotty

To be clear, "Star Trek" is no stranger to genre mashups, and they're not inherently a bad thing. Trek has been running for nearly 1,000 total episodes, and they've been doing mashups since the very first season of "Star Trek: The Original Series", which featured gangster, historical fiction, and war-themed episodes.

The holodeck took things further, giving the writers an excuse to set the action anywhere they could dream up. No more alien planets that look suspiciously like Earth were necessary to completely flip the series’ genre; just work up a hologram malfunction and suddenly "Trek" is a Sherlock Holmes-esque mystery or a noir thriller. And even without the holodeck, genres are fluid things that often take from each other to tell stories within each other’s realms.

But while "Trek" has always dabbled, it's never done an entire season of genre episodes… in fact, that might be unprecedented in all of science fiction TV itself, let alone "Star Trek". This season of "SNW" didn’t use occasional gimmicks to take a break from space fare; it was all gimmick, all the time.

Check out the episode rundown below:

  • Episode 1: Dinosaur adventure/western (Land of the Lost)
  • Episode 2: Space horror (Event Horizon)
  • Episode 3: Raunchy comedy (The Hangover)
  • Episode 4: Wartime drama (Casablanca)*
  • Episode 5: Puppets (The Muppets)
  • Episode 6: Disaster movie/real-time story (The Poseidon Adventure)
  • Episode 7: Soap opera (Days of Our Lives)
  • Episode 8: Cold War film/submarine movie (The Hunt for Red October)
  • Episode 9: Fairytale fantasy (Anything with a dragon)
  • Episode 10: Star Trek (Yes, this episode was basically SNW mashing up with TOS, and we're counting that).

* Some of you are screaming that Episode 4 was a noir. It was not. Not everything in black and white with fedoras is noir.

"Strange New Worlds" season 4 was genre-blending at scale. This wasn’t a hint of another genre influencing the episode; it was full-blown immersion into each and every one.

In the past, when other genres have come into "Trek", the series still felt tonally consistent; the characters never bent to the will of the genre, and its direction stayed the same. That was not true of this season. Characters, directorial style, and tone all bent to the will of the selected genre instead of fitting into the already established universe. There were multiple episodes this season that felt nothing like a "Star Trek" episode.

Also — and I may be in the minority here — there were only two episodes this season that I’d argue were executed well (Episode 6 and Episode 8), meaning that the relentless gimmicks paraded out each week felt not just detrimental to the show itself, but they weren’t much fun to watch either.

To go where everyone has gone before

The real question that crops up from this season is why they did it at all. If you listen to the show’s producers, it’s because they love "Trek" so much and they thought it would help move the characters along.

He is, of course, absolutely correct; that is exactly what "Trek" has traditionally used genre episodes for. When "The Original Series" went to the Nazi planet, it was one of the first and earliest examples of directly confronting fascism and Nazism on American television. When the show played with Greek gods, it took the moment to have a groundbreaking interracial kiss. Even when it went broad comedy in “The Trouble with Tribbles,” it at least kept its characters consistent and its universe coherent.

For the most part, that practice continued throughout classic "Trek" and even into the modern era, with genre being used to aid storytelling, not overwhelm it.

Season 4 of "Strange New Worlds" does none of this. It isn’t using genre as elevation; it’s using it as a distraction: a shiny gloss over a collection of episodes too afraid to say anything that will get the series accused of being “woke” or progressive. Later in the interview, Goldman claims that they can’t please everyone, but that seems like exactly what they were trying to do this season-- resulting, of course, in pleasing no one.

This season is running scared from the current moment, and it’s doing so by hiding behind gimmicks. Any previous series of "Trek" (or any great science fiction) would be tackling subjects such as immigration, fascism, war, or any other societal issue that is overwhelming us right now, but "SNW" is doing none of that, instead presenting farcical genre fare

Fear exists for one purpose; to be conquered

It’s hard not to draw a direct line from this approach to the purchase of Paramount by Skydance last year and the company’s new leadership, who are more than cozy with President Donald Trump. There seems to be little other reason that a franchise and series that were being bashed for being “too woke” and overly progressive would veer so hard into gimmickry that barely hides the hollow shell this show has become.

Rewatching the first three seasons of "SNW" shows how hard a turn this series has taken since the re-election of Trump and the steady march of companies trying to kowtow to a government that wants to squash progressive ideology.

The show has gone from telling powerful stories for both its characters and society to a series of running gags that do little more than slap the Federation delta onto people’s chests so people think it's still "Star Trek".

It isn’t. This season of nothingness is exactly what you get when you ask "Trek" not to push boundaries, not to be hopeful, not to be bold, and not to progress forward. When a show founded on speaking out and saying something spends an entire season running away from doing just that, it’s not just a condemnation of the show itself; it’s a condemnation of the creative process behind it.

The real issue with this season isn’t the attempt to play in genre for ten episodes straight; it’s that the reason they did it was fear, not hope.

   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/konec-zivota-na-zamku-deti-z-domovu-v-libereckem-kraji-dostavaji-nove-bydleni/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Místo života na zámku vlastní pokoj v rodinném domě, běžné sousedské vztahy a kamarádi v okolí. Liberecký kraj postupně mění způsob péče o děti z dětských domovů.    <title>V Česku se od poloviny tohoto týdne ochladí, objeví se přeháňky</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/pocasi/v-cesku-se-od-poloviny-tohoto-tydne-ochladi-objevi-se-prehanky/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=pocasi</link>
   <description>Česko čeká v tomto týdnu typické podzimní počasí. Pondělí a úterý mají být ještě slunečné a relativně teplé, od středy se ale zatáhne, ochladí a objeví se přeháňky. Ve druhé polovině týdne tak už budou maximální denní teploty pouze kolem deseti stupňů, ráno budou klesat i k bodu mrazu. Vyplývá to z informací Českého hydrometeorologického ústavu (ČHMÚ).</description>

 <description>Bývalá velvyslankyně Spojených arabských emirátů při OSN, Lana Nusseibehová, oznámila kandidaturu na post generální tajemnice Organizace spojených národů.  <description>Policie v 26 evropských zemích včetně Česka podnikla společnou operaci proti přeshraniční kriminalitě, při které zajistila mimo jiné 710 automobilů, 34 lodí či přes 7,4 tuny kokainu.  <description>Brazilský nejvyšší soud oznámil, že Lula da Silva v prezidentských volbách zvítězil s 51,8 procenta hlasů.  <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/eu-planuje-ukrajine-pujcit-11-bilionu-korun-cesko-i-slovensko-se-na-podpore-opet_2610260923_aru</link>
 <description>Členské státy EU chtějí do konce roku dosáhnout dohody o nové půjčce na podporu Ukrajiny v hodnotě přibližně 45 miliard eur (1,1 bilionu korun), napsal server Politico s odvoláním na své diplomatické zdroje. Půjčka, za kterou by ručil současný rozpočet EU, se rýsuje jako nejpravděpodobnější varianta, jak by Evropa mohla pokrýt finanční potřeby Ukrajiny v roce 2027.  <description>Jak se přijímají rozhodnutí v Evropské unii a proč je někdy tak těžké najít shodu? To si mohou studenti vyzkoušet v modelovém Evropském parlamentu. Na mezinárodním setkání v Praze mladí lidé z několika evropských zemí debatovali třeba o dostupnosti bydlení, lidských právech nebo umělé inteligenci. Zkušenosti z podobných simulací je učí nejen lépe rozumět politice, ale i naslouchat ostatním a spolupracovat, popisují v pořadu Bruselské chlebíčky.</description>

Stejně důležité je ale mluvit také o možnostech léčby pro ženy, které už si tuto diagnózu vyslechly.</description></item><item><title>Přijďte zažít ten nejhezčí moment roku: Kdy se v Liberci poprvé rozzáří vánoční strom?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904052-vanocni-strom-dorazi-k-liberecke-radnici-17-listopadu-rozsviti-se-v-patek-20-11.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904052-vanocni-strom-dorazi-k-liberecke-radnici-17-listopadu-rozsviti-se-v-patek-20-11.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:56:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Liberec se chystá na advent. Dominantou náměstí Dr. E. Beneše se stane 14,5 metru vysoký smrk ze Selské ulice, který 17. listopadu přivezou a ukotví dobrovolní hasiči. Slavnostní rozsvícení proběhne 20. listopadu v 17:00 a vánoční trhy odstartují 26. listopadu.</description></item><item><title>Českou Lípu povede koalice vítězného uskupení Živá Lípa, ODS a Společně</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/904047-ceskou-lipu-povede-koalice-vitezneho-uskupeni-ziva-lipa-ods-a-spolecne.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/904047-ceskou-lipu-povede-koalice-vitezneho-uskupeni-ziva-lipa-ods-a-spolecne.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 10:43:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Českou Lípu povede koalice vítězného uskupení Živá Lípa s ODS a Společně, ke kterým se připojili tři zastupitelé původně zvolení za ANO. Starostou bude Jakub Mencl z Živé Lípy.</description></item><item><title>V polovině týdne přijde ochlazení, objeví se déšť nebo přeháňky</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904046-v-polovine-tydne-prijde-ochlazeni-objevi-se-dest-nebo-prehanky.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904046-v-polovine-tydne-prijde-ochlazeni-objevi-se-dest-nebo-prehanky.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:02:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Česko čeká v tomto týdnu typické podzimní počasí. Dnešek a úterý mají být ještě slunečné a relativně teplé, od středy se ale zatáhne, ochladí a objeví se přeháňky. Ve druhé polovině týdne tak už budou maximální denní teploty pouze kolem deseti stupňů, ráno budou klesat i k bodu mrazu.</description></item><item><title>Těžká nehoda ve Stráži pod Ralskem. Řidička vjela pod náklaďák</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/904022-tezka-nehoda-ve-strazi-pod-ralskem-ridicka-vjela-pod-nakladak.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/904022-tezka-nehoda-ve-strazi-pod-ralskem-ridicka-vjela-pod-nakladak.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 06:43:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>K vážné nehodě došlo ve Stráži pod Ralskem. Řidička osobního auta nedala přednost náklaďáku a vjela mu přímo do cesty. Při nehodě utrpěla těžké zranění. Nehoda se stala v úseku, kde loni došlo ke změně přednosti.</description></item><item><title>Hokejisté Liberce porazili Plzeň 2:0, Kváča udržel potřetí v sezoně nulu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/904031-hokejiste-liberce-porazili-plzen-2-0-kvaca-udrzel-potreti-v-sezone-nulu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/904031-hokejiste-liberce-porazili-plzen-2-0-kvaca-udrzel-potreti-v-sezone-nulu.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 19:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Hokej</category><description>Hokejisté Liberce porazili ve 14. kole extraligy Plzeň 2:0 a v domácím prostředí si připsali čtvrtou výhru za sebou. Třetím čistým kontem se pod ni podepsal brankář Petr Kváča. Vítěznou branku vstřelil v 51. minutě Jakub Rychlovský, pojistku přidal trefou do opuštěné branky Martin Faško-Rudáš.</description></item><item><title>Paradox českého trhu: Firmy hledají lidi, ale padesátníkům zavírají dveře</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903857-paradox-ceskeho-trhu-firmy-hledaji-lidi-ale-padesatnikum-zaviraji-dvere.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903857-paradox-ceskeho-trhu-firmy-hledaji-lidi-ale-padesatnikum-zaviraji-dvere.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 17:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Český pracovní trh čelí paradoxu: zaměstnavatelé si stěžují na kritický nedostatek kvalifikovaných lidí, ale při náboru často staví bariéru kvůli věku. Podle průzkumu projektu Neviditelní připouštějí dvě třetiny firem, že vyšší věk uchazeče může negativně ovlivnit jeho šance na přijetí.</description></item><item><title>Jablonec po dvou gólech Nebyly vyhrál v Hradci, domácí přišli o zraněného Daridu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/904019-jablonec-po-dvou-golech-nebyly-vyhral-v-hradci-domaci-prisli-o-zraneneho-daridu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/904019-jablonec-po-dvou-golech-nebyly-vyhral-v-hradci-domaci-prisli-o-zraneneho-daridu.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 15:20:44 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Fotbalisté Jablonce zvítězili ve 12. kole první ligy v Hradci Králové 2:1. Hosty poslal ve 34. minutě do vedení z penalty Sebastian Nebyla, krátce po změně stran slovenský záložník zvýšil. Utkání zdramatizoval Tomáš Čvančara, na vyrovnání však domácí nedosáhli a navíc přišli o zraněného kapitána.</description></item><item><title>Laskavost si zaslouží ocenění. Kraj chce vyzdvihnout ty, kteří pomáhají</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903933-laskavost-si-zaslouzi-oceneni-kraj-chce-vyzdvihnout-ty-kteri-pomahaji.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903933-laskavost-si-zaslouzi-oceneni-kraj-chce-vyzdvihnout-ty-kteri-pomahaji.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 15:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Zuzana Pešková</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Velká část pomoci druhým se odehrává mimo pozornost veřejnosti. Doma, v sociálních službách i v terénu. Právě proto vznikla Cena laskavosti, kterou chce Liberecký kraj a Regionální dobrovolnické centrum poděkovat lidem, jimž není lhostejné jejich okolí. Nominace může podávat i veřejnost.</description></item></channel></rss>
